key_types.name: ComputeJob
key_types.what: inputs, published data and ComputeDomain handed to the caller's runner

key_types.name: ComputeDomain

key_types.name: WebhookPayload

read_first.why: builder: defaults (1 job, 10 MiB body, 120 s body timeout) and the zero-capacity check
route table: POST /run_compute and the health check

the background job: runner, ciphertext commitment, webhook payload

rust_patterns.note: an admitted job runs as a detached task that owns its semaphore permit
the semaphore is shared with Arc::clone, and a permit is taken with try_acquire_owned so a busy server answers at once
a failed webhook client build gets a message through .context
per-commitment work is collected into one Result, so the first bad entry fails the request

units.tests: cargo test -p e3-program-server. In-crate tests: lib.rs from line 712 (callback URL rules, localhost rewrite, builder limits, and the 408 stalled-upload, 429 full-server and 413 oversized-body responses) and types.rs (webhook serialization).
unverified: Callback filtering checks literal addresses and hostnames, not resolved/pinned sockets; DNS rebinding remains possible (lib.rs:305-386). Loopback is deliberately allowed, and operator-configured localhost rewrites bypass the private-host check.
Whether a deployment puts this server behind authentication is outside this crate; no auth layer is configured in it.
